claims.claim_text: Krungthai Bank, one of Thailand’s domestic systemically important banks (D-SIBs) designated by the Bank of Thailand (BOT), has constantly been contributing to addressing and dealing with the country’s challenges, which is in alignment with the Bank’s vision of 'Growing Together for Sustainability.'
claims.section: Message from the Chairman and CEO

claims.claim_text: We collaborate with stakeholders across all sectors to provide responsible lending, address sustainability issues, and implement human rights practices.
claims.section: Message from the Chairman and CEO

claims.claim_text: Our efforts include tackling informal and household debt through debt restructuring policies, the 'You Fight, We Help' program to support vulnerable groups, and the Sustainable Civil Servant Debt Consolidation Scheme.
claims.section: Message from the Chairman and CEO

claims.claim_text: We have also introduced a Sustainable Lending Policy.
claims.section: Message from the Chairman and CEO

claims.claim_text: The Board of Directors and Executives have worked together to develop policies, strategic plans, and business strategies to support Thailand’s transition and its path towards achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions.
claims.section: Message from the Chairman and CEO

claims.claim_text: A Green Financing Framework has been established to ensure the development and provision of sustainable finance solutions for our customers and citizens.
claims.section: Message from the Chairman and CEO

claims.claim_text: We have set a target to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions for Scope 1 and 2 across all our premises by 2030.
claims.section: Message from the Chairman and CEO

claims.claim_text: We collaborate with stakeholders to develop climate transition plans in alignment with the finance and banking sector to achieve net-zero emissions by 2065, as outlined in the national climate action plan.
claims.section: Message from the Chairman and CEO

claims.claim_text: We are determined to connect the country's infrastructure by integrating digital and financial innovations to enhance societal connectivity and support equitable and inclusive access to financial services.
claims.section: Message from the Chairman and CEO

claims.claim_text: As a result of these efforts, we have been recognized for our progress and achievements by renowned organizations worldwide, receiving a total of 88 awards—64 from international organizations and 24 from local ones.

In 2024, Krungthai Bank remained committed to emphasize operations covering three dimensions (Outcome, Enablers, and Foundation) and five strategic focuses.
The Bank aimed to accelerate execution to enhance competitive capabilities and seize future business growth opportunities through the following key initiatives.

Emphasizing an end-to-end view across the value chain, the Bank delivers products and services as total solutions while enhancing financial access for grassroots segments to reduce inequality and ensuring appropriate risk management.
The Bank accelerated the adoption of data and technology to enhance operational processes through process digitalization to improve operational speed as well as efficiency and reduce paper usage.
The Bank developed new platforms to comprehensively meet customer needs and improve access to funding and financial services for individuals across all social segments.
Krungthai Bank advanced its business under ESG principles and expanded financial access to the grassroots, especially the underbanked populations.

The Bank strengthened enterprise risk management by enhancing its effectiveness and responsiveness and also enhanced data analytics capabilities to better understand customer needs and progress toward personalized banking across channels.
Krungthai Bank invested in modern, stable, secure, and efficient IT and digital infrastructure to support growing user demand and ensure scalability for future operations.
The Bank fostered the “Courage to Change” mindset, emphasizing the need to adopt flexible and responsive work practices grounded in the “Fail Fast, Learn Fast” principle.

The Bank is committed to creating opportunities for all Thai citizens to access financial resources comprehensively, reducing inequality and strengthening the economy at all levels to enhance the well-being and quality of life of people through Thailand’s Open Digital Platform.
The Bank is committed to integrating sustainability into all aspects of its operations and fostering a culture of sustainability across the organization.
In 2024, the Bank designated the Sustainability Management Committee as the driving force behind sustainability performance.

Krungthai Bank has consistently issued annual Sustainability Reports since 2006 to communicate our commitment to responsible social operations and its progress in managing efforts to reduce impacts on the economy, society, environment, and human rights, while also enhancing transparent governance.
This report discloses the Bank's performance from January 1 to December 31, 2024, in accordance with the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards 2021.

It is also the first year that the IFRS S1 General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial Information, set by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), have been applied to enhance sustainability performance reporting.

The Bank has adopted the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) standards for the commercial bank industry as a guideline for disclosing information and performance in accordance with international standards.
The Bank has integrated the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into its operations.
It complies with the principles of the United Nations Global Compact to demonstrate its commitment to achieving sustainable development goals.
In 2024, Krungthai Bank conducted the Sustainability Materiality Assessment in alignment with the Double Materiality Assessment Approach through the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards 2021.

The assessment comprehensively reveals the sustainability factors, risks, and opportunities that align with the IFRS S1 General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial Information.
A total of 13 materiality topics were identified, covering the governance, environmental, and social dimensions.

The Bank transparently collects and discloses information regarding management, targets, and performances in accordance with stakeholder expectations, referencing external assessment guidelines such as the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB), Thailand Taxonomy (Phase I), S&P Global, and FTSE Russell.
The changes in the assessment of key issues in 2024 have resulted in a slight adjustment in the Bank's financial impact compared to the previous year.
The Bank is committed to operating efficiently, transparently, and responsibly with respect to its stakeholders.
The Bank has developed stringent cybersecurity measures, along with strict protection of customer data privacy.
Financial institutions play a key role in driving efforts to mitigate the impact of climate change.
Establishing a strategy for achieving net zero greenhouse gas emissions is a crucial issue in the banking sector.
The Bank focuses on improving the quality of life for individuals and supporting the sustainable growth of Thailand's economy, ensuring that no one is left behind.

The Bank has analyzed and prioritized stakeholders and determined the engagement approaches for each group of stakeholders to ensure appropriate, efficient, and fair treatment of all stakeholders as outlined in the Bank’s policy on good corporate governance and Code of Conduct.

The Sustainability Management Committee is responsible for reviewing information and the outcomes of the Bank's engagement with stakeholders, and reports this to the Corporate Governance and Sustainability Committee.
Treat employees fairly and appropriately, and respect their rights according to human rights principles and human resource management practices of the Bank.
Promote good health and well-being of employees by providing various facilities.
Provide a working environment that is safe, hygienic, and conducive to work.
Develop and offer products and services to meet the needs of each customer sector.
Resolve complaints according to Service Level Agreement (SLA).
Strictly comply with the law and operate according to the principles of good corporate governance.
Take feedback from regulators and make adaptations and improvements accordingly to meet international standards.
Consider the positive and negative impact on society and the environment, which is part of the Bank’s performance evaluation.

Drive transformation with waves of new ideas to deliver comprehensive green financial solutions that meet global standards, accelerating the transition to a low-carbon society and contributing to restoring environmental balance.

claims.claim_text: The Bank recognizes its critical role in driving Thailand towards a low-carbon economy, in alignment with our vision: ‘Growing Together for Sustainability’.
The Bank has defined roles and responsibilities at the Board and senior management levels to oversee climate change initiatives.

The Board of Directors is responsible for setting the direction for managing climate-related risks and strategies and for reviewing the Bank's operations and performance in relation to its commitments, targets and indicators.

The Corporate Governance and Sustainability Committee is tasked with developing and implementing climate-related strategies and policies, including decisions on investments, lending and risk management.
The Sustainability Management Committee operates at an operational level, playing a role in monitoring the development of sustainability policies from all sectors.

Various divisions, including the Cluster/Business Units, Risk Cluster, Operations, Sustainability Unit and business units at all levels of the Bank, are responsible for supporting sustainability-related data and initiatives within the company.
To ensure the plans are practical, the Bank considers the engagement and feedback of all stakeholders, especially the practitioners.
The Bank prioritises climate-related issues and adheres to practices that align with the vision ‘Growing Together for Sustainability’.
We have integrated social and environmental responsibility into the organizational structure and approaches that adhere to international environmental, social and governance (ESG) standards.
The Bank has developed climate change strategies in accordance with the recommendations from the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).
The Bank has developed a strategy to achieve Krungthai's Pathway to Net Zero.

claims.claim_text: As the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from lending and investments is part of the Krungthai Pathway to Net Zero project, the operations are driven by the Sustainability Management Committee and the Product Committee.

The formulation of strategies and policies under the Krungthai Pathway to Net Zero aims to become a net-zero greenhouse gas emission organization, addressing risks and expectations from all stakeholders.
The Bank has initiated the development of a Transition Plan, supported by the Bank of Thailand and in collaboration with the Thai Bankers' Association.

This transition plan serves as a crucial mechanism for businesses and the Bank, setting targets, operational guidelines and timelines for businesses to adapt and achieve greenhouse gas reduction goals.

In developing the transition plan, the Bank considers relevant domestic regulations and guidelines, such as standard practices or environmental operation standards for financial institutions (standard practice) and the Thailand taxonomy for economic activity classification.
From the Bank's preliminary study, we found that the power generation sector has the highest greenhouse gas emissions, and the highest outstanding loan value compared to the Bank's credit portfolio.
claims.section: Portfolio Analysis to Consider Business Sectors that are Priority Sectors

claims.claim_text: The Bank sets environmental targets for executives and employees at all levels, including overall departmental goals, to effectively and continuously implement policies and measures for resource and environmental management.
Commitment to achieving Net Zero greenhouse gas emissions in Scope 1 and 2 by 2030.
Reduce greenhouse gas emissions in Scopes 1 and 2 by 18% by 2024, compared to the baseline from 2022.
The organization achieved a significant reduction in total energy consumption from 2021 to 2023, but saw a slight increase (+0.12%) in 2024.
Energy intensity per FTE peaked in 2022, then returned to 2021 levels by 2023 and remained steady in 2024.
There is a clear downward trend in both total and disposed waste from 2021 to 2024.
The amount of reused and recycled waste increases each year, suggesting improved recycling efforts.

The Bank has established an ‘Energy Conservation and Technology Committee’ working group responsible for promoting, monitoring, and overseeing energy conservation efforts, as well as integrating new technology and innovations into work processes.
The Bank has set up a ‘Sustainability Management Committee’ to promote and support the Bank's sustainability initiatives and ensure they are in compliance with international standards.

Krungthai Bank recognizes the importance of promoting financial inclusion and financial literacy, not just for the bank's economic benefit but also for sustainable development and creating a more equitable society.
The Bank is committed to enhancing financial literacy in areas such as savings planning, spending, and investing, to promote well-being and reduce the occurrence of bad debts.

The Bank is committed to supporting access to financial services for various groups through the Krungthai NEXT and Paotang applications, as well as by expanding programs and activities for financial literacy and digital technology.

In 2024, the Bank has set a target to increase the number of participants in face-to-face training with hands-on practice to 3,000 people, including vulnerable groups, youth, small entrepreneurs, low-income groups, women, the elderly, and those in remote areas.
The Bank aims to have 200 participants in focus groups promoting the habit of saving from 10 universities nationwide.
Total reach for financial knowledge and digital technology usage through social media is 34 million reaches and had a deep participation of 1 million times (engagement).
The Bank prioritizes addressing the needs of all groups, ensuring that no one is left behind or restricted in their rights to access financial services or knowledge.
claims.section: Impacts to the Economy, Environment, Society and Human Rights

claims.claim_text: The Bank emphasizes sustainable development by operating responsibly towards society and committing to enhancing financial knowledge and access for all groups.
The Bank ensures that visually impaired users can perform financial transactions independently and efficiently by utilizing the VoiceOver function on iOS and TalkBack on Android devices.
The application reduces inequality in financial service access and promotes eco-friendly business through paperless transactions.
This supports the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and aligns with the Bank’s vision of 'Growing Together for Sustainability'.
In 2024, the Bank partnered with the Department of Land Transport to provide international driving licenses through the Paotang application.
The Krungthai debit card is a financial product issued by the Bank to facilitate convenient and secure financial transactions, supporting the transition towards a cashless society.
The international money transfer service on the Krungthai NEXT application offers convenience and speed with reduced fees.
The Bank has developed an electronic letter of guarantee service (e-LG), which reduces paper usage and streamlines document submission processes, thereby mitigating the risk of lost guarantees.
The Bank integrates environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors into its lending policies, financial advisory services and investments.

claims.claim_text: The Bank has implemented sustainability measures in line with its vision, ‘Growing Together for Sustainability’, by integrating environmental and social considerations into its internal operations.

The Bank has systematically planned its ESG management by developing a transition plan for priority sectors and establishing green loan, social loan, and sustainability-linked loan criteria to meet international standards.

Krungthai Bank has developed a sustainable lending policy to demonstrate its commitment to operations that reduce negative impacts on society and the environment throughout the Bank's value chain and to prevent business operation risks.

The bank incorporates sustainable development frameworks and principles at an international level, considering its unique identity, and aligns its operations with Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principle to conduct business and deliver services responsibly for society and the environment.
The Bank is committed to developing its workforce by creating an open, supportive and growth-promoting work environment.
This includes attracting and retaining quality employees, promoting diversity and equality and fostering a responsible and unified organizational culture.

The Bank collaborates with government agencies and other organizations in proactive domestic recruitment programs, such as the Development and Promotion of Science and Technology Talents Project (DPST) and the National Science and Technology Development Agency (NSTDA) scholarship program.
In 2024, the Bank launched the following various projects to recruit high-potential young talents and enhance the image of being a modern and sustainable bank.

The Krungthai Internship initiative focuses on students in fields like computer engineering, computer science, information technology, cybersecurity and related disciplines such as innovation technology, digital technology, business analysis and data science.
This program also supports the education system and human capital development, aligning with the Bank's social responsibility goals.
In 2024, more than 40 students participated in internships with the Bank and its financial group companies. Additionally, over 200 students interned with the Bank in other specialized areas.

Management Trainee for Credit Analyst (MTCA) and Krungthai Management Trainee Programs recruit individuals with a talent for proactive business credit analysis, preparing them for business credit roles to enhance their capabilities.
The programs identify and prepare high-potential individuals to become successors in Core Banking and Digital Banking areas, aligning with the Bank's strategy and policies for digital transformation.
Employer Branding initiative aims to attract and recruit high-potential employees through various promotional activities to enhance the Bank's image.
The project emphasizes upskilling and reskilling employees, encouraging cross-collaboration and utilizing AI tools to enhance work efficiency.
It gathers 74 talented employees from various departments at Krungthai Bank, equipping them with AI skills and new working methods to become future-ready.

This also fosters cross-department collaboration to drive new ways of working and develop products and services that meet the Bank's seven strategic objectives under the Reshaping Client Value Proposition concept.
Participants will undergo diverse learning courses such as Design Thinking, Garage Model and Agile Framework, AI and Prompt, ensuring the efficiency of the chase and pushing ideas to market.

Wolf 1: Kra Shout Alert: A financial tool offering personalized AI assistance, providing tailored investment advice, personalized alerts for fund trading and professional portfolio management tools with E-solutions and AI.

Wolf 3: Vayu Co-Pilot: Uses generative AI to manage data and help employees work accurately, swiftly and up-to-date, analyzing customer needs with a Knowledge Base Center and Product Offering functions.

Wolf 2: Krungthai Near Home: Aims to transform Krungthai Bank into a community hub by upgrading government-subsidized stores to be the Bank's Banking Agents, offering elderly pension withdrawals and other financial services, with AI analyzing personalized lending models for future credit offers.

Wolf 4: Wolf Health: Develops projects with multiple partners through the Health Wallet on the Pao Tang app, enabling public access to free medication for 32 minor ailments, featuring a nearby pharmacy locator and solutions for pharmacy businesses.
Wolf 5: Biz Speed: Creates the Fast Biz Model to transform SME customer experiences, positioning Krungthai Bank as the top choice for business customers.
